Imatinib: Cc1ccc(NC(=O)c2ccc(CN3CCN(C)CC3)cc2)cc1Nc1nccc(-c2cccnc2)…
turns.responseText:
ABL1 Pharmacophore Modeling & Library Screening — Builds a consensus pharmacophore from 4 ABL1 inhibitor SMILES and screens a 4-compound library in a single integrated workflow.


Input:

reference_smiles → 4 known ABL1 inhibitors (Imatinib, Dasatinib, Bosutinib, Asciminib)
library_smiles → 4 compounds to screen (Gleevec-analog-1, Ponatinib, Terfenadine, Acetaminophen)
min_features = 3 (minimum pharmacophore features required for a hit)



Key steps:

RDKit / pharmer → Extracts H-bond donors/acceptors, hydrophobic centers, aromatic rings, and positive ionizable features from the 4 reference actives → generates a consensus pharmacophore model
Pharmacophore screening → Each library compound is mapped against the model; compounds matching ≥ 3 features are flagged as hits; match scores are computed and ranked
Report generation → Ranked hit list + feature match matrix + 2D pharmacophore map exported



Expected output:

pharmacophore_hits.csv — ranked compounds with feature match count and score
pharmacophore_model.json — serialized feature definitions (type, coordinates, tolerance)
feature_match_matrix.html — visual report showing which features each library compound satisfies
Predicted outcome: Gleevec-analog-1 and Ponatinib are expected to score as hits (structurally similar to ABL1 inhibitor scaffold); Terfenadine and Acetaminophen are expected to fail the min_features=3 threshold
